question: The teachings of Mahavira and his followers were written down about 1500 years ago in the form in which they are presently available at which place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Valabhi in Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The teachings of Mahavira and his followers were compiled and written down in the form of Jain Agamas at Valabhi in Gujarat.
 
• The Jain Agamas are canonical scriptures of Jainism and were orally transmitted for many centuries before being written down.
 
• The compilation of these teachings took place around the 5th to 6th century CE.
 
• Valabhi was an important center of Jain scholarship and education during that period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahavira:**

 
 
• Mahavira, also known as Vardhamana, was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.
 
• He was born in 599 BCE in Kundagrama, near Vaishali (now in Bihar).
 
• Mahavira preached non-violence, truth, and asceticism and is considered a reformer of the Jain community.
 
 
 
• **Jain Agamas:**
 
 
• The Jain Agamas are a collection of texts based on the teachings of Mahavira and his disciples.
 
• They form the primary scriptures of Jainism, particularly for the Svetambara sect.
 
• The Agamas were composed of various types of works such as sutras, commentaries, and philosophical texts.
 
 
 
• **Compilation at Valabhi:**
 
 
• Valabhi, located in present-day Gujarat, was a major center of learning and a hub for Jain monks and scholars.
 
• The Jain council held at Valabhi under the leadership of Devardhigani Kshamashramana is believed to have finalized the compilation of the Agamas.
 
• This event ensured the preservation and propagation of Jain teachings for future generations.
